record.paper_title: Open Problems in Data-Sharing Peer-to-Peer Systems
record.original_question: In a decentralized data-sharing peer-to-peer system that supports keyword queries, can one design a search mechanism that is both efficient in its use of bandwidth, processing, and storage and also comprehensive in the sense that it returns all matching results, without resorting to prohibitively expensive network-wide flooding?

evidence.quote: Hence, designing techniques for efficient, comprehensive search remains an open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a decentralized peer-to-peer network modeled as a dynamic graph G=(V,E) whose vertices are autonomous peers, each holding a local collection of data objects annotated with sets of keywords. Peers communicate only by sending messages along edges of G; no peer has global knowledge of V, E, or of the data held by other peers. A keyword query is a finite set Q of keywords issued at some peer v∈V, and a result for Q is any data object (held at some peer) whose keyword annotation contains every keyword in Q. A search mechanism is a distributed protocol that, given a query Q at v, returns a set R(Q,v) of results to v.

Call a search mechanism comprehensive if, for every query Q and every issuing peer v, R(Q,v) equals the set of all results for Q present anywhere in the network at query time. Call the mechanism efficient if the total number of messages exchanged, the per-peer processing cost, and the per-peer auxiliary storage are each bounded by a function that grows strictly sub-linearly (e.g., polylogarithmically) in |V| and in the total number of data objects, uniformly over queries and network states. Flooding (broadcasting the query to every reachable peer) is excluded as it is not efficient under this definition.

Question: Does there exist a distributed search mechanism for keyword queries on such a peer-to-peer network that is simultaneously comprehensive and efficient in the above sense, or can it be proved that no such mechanism exists?
artifact.status_search_result: The question, posed as an open problem in the area of data-sharing P2P systems, asks whether efficient and comprehensive keyword search can coexist in fully decentralized networks. A search of subsequent literature on distributed keyword search (DHT-based indexing, Bloom-filter routing, semantic overlays, gossip-based search) shows ongoing work providing partial trade-offs (efficient but approximate/incomplete, or comprehensive but costly), but no published result that simultaneously achieves both for general decentralized P2P keyword search. The problem appears to remain open.
